summary: FASE 1 P0 — Cross-user isolation of /api/tutor/exam-feedback validated end-to-end against live backend with real LLM generation. 6/6 tests passed (48s). User A and User B, authenticated via /api/auth/dev-login with distinct emails, POSTed the identical Devolutiva payload; both received HTTP 200 with 10 questions and DIFFERENT feedback.content_id — no cache leak. Same user A reposting the same payload correctly received content_source='reused' with the identical content_id, confirming intra-user cache still works. Response shape (diagnosis, focus_areas[], questions[10], content_id, content_source) is intact.
critical_code_review_comments: exam_feedback_key_fields() correctly includes user_id in the key fields dict, and compute_fingerprint_generic() folds all key_fields into the SHA — so fingerprints are per-user by construction. Verified via both deterministic and live E2E tests.
Intra-user reuse works via _lookup_active(fp) returning the same content_id, and content_source='reused' is surfaced to the client.
test_credentials: dev-login open with ENABLE_DEV_LOGIN=true. Users used: phase1_userA@medflow.local / phase1_userB@medflow.local.
seed_data_creation: Two dev users A and B created via /api/auth/dev-login. Two exam_feedback content records generated (one per user) plus one intra-user reuse.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 1 P0 GO. New live E2E test at /app/backend/tests/test_phase1_devolutiva_e2e.py runs in ~50s and asserts (1) different content_id for A vs B on identical payloads and (2) intra-user reuse yields content_source='reused' with same content_id. Re-run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_phase1_devolutiva_e2e.py -v
rca of the issue: N/A — no issue. Isolation confirmed at both the fingerprint layer (deterministic test) and the HTTP layer (E2E test hitting live LLM-backed endpoint).
